faq.a: No. It is two municipalities — the District of North Vancouver, governed District-wide by OCP Bylaw 7900, and the City of North Vancouver, guided by OCP Bylaw, 2014, No. 8400 — with separate councils, bylaws and taxes.

faq.q: How do residents reach downtown Vancouver without a car?
faq.a: The SeaBus sails from Lonsdale Quay at the foot of Lonsdale Avenue to Waterfront Station in Vancouver, and buses meet the ferry at the Lonsdale Quay exchange.

faq.q: Which school district serves North Vancouver, and how do catchments work?
faq.a: School District 44 serves both municipalities, with no middle tier (elementary K–7, secondary 8–12). Catchments are address-based and must be confirmed with the district for the exact address.

Lions Gate Hospital, 231 East 15th Street in the City of North Vancouver, operated by Vancouver Coastal Health, serves the North Shore; urgent and primary care is at 221 West Esplanade in Lower Lonsdale.

faq.q: Why are District and City prices so different?
faq.a: They are different housing stocks and different income bases: the City is the condo/apartment corridor and the District is predominantly detached houses, and the 2021 Census median household income was $86,000 in the City versus $123,000 in the District (Statistics Canada, 2021 Census Profile).
